items.title: Migrate the five active reviewer role prompts behind independent rollback flags
items.context: Move concept, quality, test-coverage, behavior, and docs to modular role assets; retired channel must remain excluded and legacy-full-context must remain readable.

happy.desc: Exactly concept, quality, test-coverage, behavior, and docs resolve to versioned modular Role Contracts and trusted prompt assembly when each role flag is enabled; each role keeps its existing reviewer lane identity, commands, stop conditions, and finding/pass authority.

Each of the five active reviewer roles has an independent rollback flag whose enabled and disabled states select modular and legacy assembled prompts only for that role, with no cross-role flag coupling.

Registry and default dispatch report the five migrated roles as active while lattice-review-channel remains retired, defaultDispatch=false, absent from active counts, wave budgets, assurance floor, receipt, and quorum collection.

With a role flag disabled, the role can still execute through the legacy assembled prompt and existing envelope-less historical reviewer artifacts remain readable only as legacy-full-context in their recorded round.

edge.desc: All mixed flag combinations are supported: any subset of the five roles may use modular prompts while the rest use legacy prompts, and every lane retains its own contract and evidence identity.
Missing, malformed, duplicated, or unknown per-role flag configuration fails to the documented legacy-safe state or an explicit error; it never silently enables another role or retired channel.
Compatibility roles remain explicitly callable only under their compatibility contract and are excluded from active role counts and default reviewer waves without being incorrectly retired.

A role-by-role baseline diff proves required sections, forbidden actions, allowed commands, stop conditions, lane identity, and current authority are preserved; any semantic deletion blocks approval even when rendered text is shorter.

adversarial.desc: Direct, aliased, mixed-case, or flag-assisted attempts to dispatch lattice-review-channel for a new review are explicitly rejected and cannot fall through to an active role.
Changing one role flag, agentType, registry index, or cached prompt cannot cause another role contract or prompt to be served; role, contract, and envelope digests must agree.
A valid-looking pass or finding from retired or compatibility roles cannot satisfy any active lane, current-round receipt, assurance floor, delivery check, or quorum requirement.

Concurrent role migrations, rollback requests, and baseline approvals cannot lose updates or produce a hybrid registry or baseline; shared writes use the main write lock while lane evidence remains signed and lane scoped.

items.title: Assemble trusted full or eligible incremental reviewer Prompt Envelopes
items.context: Reuse Story 2 full-envelope provenance and Story 4 fail-closed eligibility; contract, policy, scope, freshness, or authority drift must deterministically select full.

happy.desc: For each of concept, quality, test-coverage, behavior, and docs, full mode is assembled in the trusted launch process and binds the exact Runtime Contract, role-specific Role Contract, current task context, known environment, assembler and launcher digests, current HEAD/material/storyFiles hashes, and signed ReviewRun.

For each active reviewer role, only Story 4 mechanically eligible metadata-only or fully bound pure-fixture deltas produce an incremental Prompt Envelope with exact lane, prior-pass, freshness, reviewBasis, changed/impacted file, intent, contract, and context digests.

Contract, policy, scope, required-lane, authority, permission, source, docs, public schema/API/protocol, dependency/build, unknown-impact, or stale material drift deterministically selects full for the affected role with stable reason codes.

An incremental reviewer can read current authoritative references and request a new full-context ReviewRun with a recorded reason; the original incremental run is not silently mutated or accepted as full.

edge.desc: Incremental baseline requires the latest valid PASS from the same role lane, same review round, signed ReviewRun, intact Prompt Envelope, and canonical freshness classification; wrong-lane, older, stale, unsigned, or envelope-less evidence selects full.

Role or Runtime semanticDigest and agent-facing renderDigest changes invalidate incremental reuse, while only metadata proven absent from model input may retain eligibility under the canonical freshness reader.

Safety eligibility is decided before size: eligible incremental wins only when under its budget and smaller than full; equal/larger uses FULL_CHEAPER_OR_EQUAL, oversize incremental selects full, and correctness-required oversize full remains full with budgetViolation=full.

A pre-migration pass without the new Prompt Envelope remains legacy-full-context, readable only in its original round, and can never become an incremental baseline through defaults, backfill, or a newly enabled role flag.

adversarial.desc: Main, implementer, reviewer, config, or CLI arguments such as contextMode, forceIncremental, fabricated impacted files, or claimed reason codes cannot override authoritative full selection for any role.

Mutating role ID, contract/context/reviewBasis digest, eligibility decision, freshness class, changed files, selection reason, ReviewRun binding, signature, or assembled prompt after launch invalidates pass, finding admission, collector credit, receipt, floor, and quorum.
During mixed rollback, an incremental or full envelope for one active role cannot be replayed as another role, and a legacy prompt cannot be paired with a modular envelope or vice versa.

Concurrent reviewers, flag changes, baseline writes, or material changes cannot combine eligibility from one snapshot with contracts or task context from another; stale or hybrid runs are rejected and require fresh full assembly.

items.title: Prove per-role quality and input reduction with preregistered replay
items.context: Use Story 3 replay/usage harness; require seeded critical/high detection or mark INCONCLUSIVE, report per-role assembled tokens, and require at least 50% incremental-context reduction with a 40% initial assembled-prompt target.

happy.desc: Before execution, freeze at least two historical Stories from each required class, the five reviewer roles, legacy-full/modular-full/modular-incremental arms, model/tool/material envelope, run order or seed support, at least three repetitions per applicable cell, and an independent adjudicated finding oracle.

Per role and applicable Story, every critical seeded finding is detected and no independently confirmed systematic high-severity miss occurs; findings match by stable semantic category plus source/claim binding rather than wording.

For every eligible role/sample cell with valid comparable measurements, modular incremental context input tokens are reported against modular full context and demonstrate at least 50 percent reduction; non-eligible cells are not used in the denominator.

Actual dispatched assembled-prompt tokens are reported separately for all five roles and compared with each role baseline; the initial target is at least 40 percent reduction, with target misses reported honestly rather than averaged away.

edge.desc: Missing historical material, invalid or empty seeded denominator, arm asymmetry, fewer than required samples/repetitions, version drift, ambiguous high miss, or unavailable independent adjudication yields INCONCLUSIVE and no claim that recall is preserved.

Input, output, cache-read, cache-creation, uncached, latency, and provider-processed usage are reported per host and role when observed; unsupported or zero-but-unobserved fields are unavailable(reason), not fabricated zero or inferred from assembled size.

Provider seed support, controllable sampling parameters, run order, retries, failures, and model/contract versions are recorded; lack of deterministic seed does not invalidate the protocol but prevents deterministic claims beyond repeated adjudicated evidence.

Per-role replay reports independently adjudicated false positives and reviewer command misuse; prompt reduction is not accepted as quality-equivalent when either materially increases even if seeded recall and token targets pass.

adversarial.desc: Deleting, relabeling, downgrading, duplicating, or excluding a seeded critical/high finding or an applicable failed cell after results are known invalidates the replay result and produces INCONCLUSIVE.

Gross tokens, cache hits, estimator output, or aggregated wave totals cannot substitute for actual per-role assembled input and provider usage; cache categories remain separated so savings cannot be overstated.
Replay runs are read-only or sandboxed and their findings, passes, receipts, usage, and ReviewRun IDs cannot satisfy production Story review gates, floor, quorum, delivery, or DONE evidence.

Selecting only successful repetitions, changing historical material, mixing model/contract versions, reordering arms after observation, or using unequal task/tool envelopes is detected from the manifest and forces INCONCLUSIVE for affected savings and recall claims.

items.title: Preserve reviewer authority and verify rollback, compatibility, and process contracts
items.context: Run role-by-role baseline diff, approval, feature-flag rollback, old-pass compatibility, signature/permission gates, adversarial drift escalation, and documentation synchronization.
